Each sentence goes on a line of its own. Long sentences are not wrapped, however long they get, and short ones are not joined. Questions? Exclamations! Both end sentences.

Abbreviations such as e.g. and i.e. do not end one, nor do titles like Dr. Smith or Mrs. Jones, initials as in J. R. R. Tolkien, or dotted ones like U.S. Navy. A period before a lowercase word, as in no. three or approx. ten, ends nothing either.

"Quoted sentences end after the quote." *So do emphasized ones.* (And ones in parentheses.) Then the next one starts.
A soft break inside a sentence
goes away.

> Quotes and
>
> - list items. Get the same treatment.
